title: CGI-sponsored GTNews survey reveals major challenge for corporate banks—declining client satisfaction (part 2)
summary: This CGI blog post explores how technology can address declining corporate client satisfaction in banking.
body_text: In my first blog in this two-part series, I shared a key finding of The Global Treasurer’s Transaction Banking Survey (GTNews survey) for 2019—declining corporate client satisfaction. In that blog, I covered possible drivers behind this four-year decline, along with how corporate banks can respond. In this second blog, I explore the technology aspects of the corporate client-banking relationship, as well as how that relationship is evolving, alongside open banking. In 2019, as in 2018, the number one technical priority raised by corporate clients is benefitting from new technologies, including blockchain. Corporate clients want their banks to use their scale, size and reach to deliver the benefits of these new technologies to the corporate treasurer. Closely following this priority is enhancing working capital management, along with meeting new and upcoming regulations. As we expected, when it comes to technology, several emerging technology areas are just as important, and possibly even more important, than blockchain. Some of these include robotic process automation, intelligent automation, and even advanced or predictive analytics. All of these technologies, when properly applied, enable corporate banks to deliver more accurate, useful and timely information, helping corporate treasurers run their businesses more effectively. As we know from previous surveys, these technologies have been on the wish list of corporate clients for a number of years. The trend now seems to have moved from being about technology (what is it?) to being about the deliverables (how can I use it?). Corporate clients also were quick to point out in the survey that they realize there is a fine balancing act between cost and benefit. Cost is very important to them, but they also realize the importance of value, as corporate banking is very much a “you get what you pay for” type of market. The research, as in previous years, also peeks into where corporate banks are investing and where they believe they can add the most value to their corporate clients. It is interesting to see how well aligned they are to corporate client demands. The top two areas where corporate banks believe they can create competitive differentiation are acting as a long-term partner and investing in continually improving their products and services (both at 88%). Ultimately, they are focusing on providing best-in-class products and services, as well as rolling out more digital servicing to deliver a more instant—and comprehensive—customer experience. When questioned in more detail, one of our large banking clients shared that its goal is to understand individual client needs better, so that it can provide more customized services to meet their requirements, even in some cases developing custom solutions. This is an interesting development and demonstrates the flexibility built into modern systems, which enables corporate banks to adjust standard products through parameter changes rather than wholesale development. In the days of legacy systems, this would have cost millions and taken years to bring to market. It does seem that corporate banks are finally aligning themselves to the needs of their clients. For many years, we saw corporate banks investing in several areas that simply did not align with corporate client needs. This change is great news for both the banks and their clients because it means the industry can create some real traction in moving clients closer to achieving their business goals—and reverse the trend of declining satisfaction. Another key topic is open banking, which has been operating in several markets in retail banking but has not yet gained much traction in the corporate banking world. Part of the reason for this is that everyone understands the needs of the retail customer, as we are all retail customers ourselves, but few FinTechs understand corporate client needs or even how to access corporate clients. So new partnerships are developing where leading corporate banks are working with FinTechs to help them understand both the complex needs of the corporate treasurer and the regulatory minefield that applies to this market, while also providing valuable access to the corporate customer. Open banking also has been slower to take off in corporate banking because, while regulation mandates it in a number of retail banking markets, there is no regulatory mandate for corporate banking—anywhere. Therefore, many corporate banks have rightly adopted a “wait and see” strategy to assess whether open banking can provide them any meaningful value. However, this is not the case for all banks. Some market-leading players are already working closely with selected FinTechs to build partnerships that deliver innovative new products, services and concepts. As open banking in the corporate banking world takes off, it will be interesting to see if the solutions that come out of the non-mandated markets actually go further than they do in the mandated markets. It is quite likely that the non-mandated markets will have better success, as well as more innovative approaches, because banks will invest in development based on the business case rather than to simply comply with regulation. Going further, open banking in the corporate world will drive real benefits from the use of open APIs. APIs have been around for a long time, but in the corporate banking world, much of the corporate integration still takes place through batch files. As these disappear and deeper integration and automation takes place through APIs, the benefits delivered to corporate clients will increase significantly, enabling the delivery of real-time information and true integration of services into treasury management systems. Finally, the survey looked at the more general use of technology by corporate banks to deliver in real time. We see the move to real time particularly in the payments world, as more banks transition to instant payments; however, this is just the first step. Corporate treasurers have been demanding access to timely information for many years, and technology is now enabling this. In summary, while the bad news is that corporate client satisfaction is at an all-time low, the good news is that, for the first time in many years, banks more closely align with their clients’ requirements. They are investing in the solutions, innovation and services their corporate clients want and, as a result, the majority of corporate clients are sticking with their main bankers and not outsourcing services to third parties—at least for now. Overall then, the picture looks good for corporate bankers. However, to improve corporate client satisfaction levels, they are going to have to act fast and deliver on their promises. I invite you to download a free copy of the The Global Treasurer’s Transaction Banking Survey . In addition, CGI is working with corporate banks across the globe to develop and executive digital strategies and solutions to meet the growing and changing demands of corporate clients. Please feel free to contact me with any questions about our research and experiences, as well as how we might help your business.

title: Spotify’s Greasy Tunes Nairobi Brings the City’s Soundtrack to Life
summary: What happens when a familiar, everyday space becomes a stage for music, conversation, and community? That’s the idea behind Greasy Tunes, Spotify’s multi-week residency in Nairobi that brings Kenya’s listening culture off the playlist and into the real world. Inspired by the original concept of transforming a classic “greasy spoon” cafe into a cultural hub,...
body_text: What happens when a familiar, everyday space becomes a stage for music, conversation, and community? That’s the idea behind Greasy Tunes, Spotify’s multi-week residency in Nairobi that brings Kenya’s listening culture off the playlist and into the real world. Inspired by the original concept of transforming a classic “greasy spoon” cafe into a cultural hub, Spotify’s Greasy Tunes Nairobi is a 12-day program at Nairobi’s Heltz House, a community events space, with programming running July 15-26. More than anything, Greasy Tunes reminds us that music is best experienced together. From data to IRL The lineup for Greasy Tunes was built around how Nairobi listens. Spotify data from June 2026 showed that listeners 18-24 are responsible for more than half of all streams in the city. With listening peaking in the evening, music is clearly a key part of how young Nairobians unwind and connect—and Greasy Tunes is designed to capture that vibe. “Greasy Tunes brings the energy people experience on Spotify into a shared physical space,” said Agnes Opondo , Artist & Label Partnerships Lead for East Africa. “The program reflects how music already connects Nairobi’s young listeners, whether through food, conversation, creativity, or community.” Week one: A taste of the city The first week, themed “Starters,” explored the intersection of sound and culture. The Greasy Tunes Café turned Heltz House into a daytime hub for work and connection, while the week’s events showed how music is part of the city’s social rituals. The week kicked off with a Kitchen Opening Party with The BAG, a leading Nairobi music and culture platform, setting the tone by celebrating the links between food, music, and community. Karibu Night, hosted by Studio 18, a creative collective known for championing the local fashion and cultural scene, translated the sound of Spotify’s Made In Kenya playlist into a fashion showcase. The night included a live performance from BURUKLYN BOYZ , whose hip-hop and drill sound added another dimension to the Made In Kenya story. https://storage.googleapis.com/pr-newsroom-wp/1/2026/07/7.mp4 The week flowed from fashion into conversation with live podcast recordings from Culture Club , Spotify’s editor-led podcast exploring African music and culture, featuring Kenyan songwriter and producer Eric Musyoka , and The 30 Percent Podcast . Live performances also took over Heltz House, including The Fisherman’s Experience and ADUMA Presents . The week closed with Smocha Sundays, which brought together gospel music, community, and a live football watch party, showing the many ways people gather around sound. NEXT Week two: The main course The second week, “Mains,” expands to focus on the way music fuels creative practice. It kicked off with Gufy’s Room: Poetry, Music & Storytelling, a live performance blending spoken word, music, and storytelling from Kenyan poet and filmmaker Gufy , and continued with a behind-the-scenes look at the creative process with a workshop where Kasi Flavour championed women in music, and a fan event with songwriter and rapper Nyashinski . Experiences still to come include an EQUAL workshop and showcase with Ongeza Volume , a community platform spotlighting Kenya’s music ecosystem, and a comedy night with The Standup Collective. It all wraps up with the Strictly Soul: Closing Party at the end of the week. The ongoing event makes one thing clear: for young Nairobians, music isn’t just something they stream. It’s a fundamental part of life and community in their city. Explore the sounds of Nairobi with Spotify’s Made In Kenya , an Afropop-led editorial playlist celebrating the artists shaping Kenya’s sound.

title: How to Prioritize Sales Coaching in 2026
summary: Every frontline sales manager faces the same challenge: you have a team of reps, and only so many hours in the week to coach them. This guide gives you a repeatable system for coaching prioritization so you can direct your time where it moves the needle most.
body_text: Every frontline sales manager faces the same challenge: you have a team of eight, ten, or fifteen reps, and only so many hours in the week to coach them . Who gets your attention first? Without a clear answer, coaching becomes reactive. You focus on whoever missed quota last month, whoever flagged a deal in the pipeline review, or whoever asked for help loudest. That approach leaves gaps. The reps who quietly need support often stay invisible, while high performers absorb coaching time they don't necessarily require. This guide gives you a repeatable system for coaching prioritization so you can direct your time where it moves the needle most. Key Takeaways: How to Prioritize Sales Coaching in 2026 Coaching prioritization starts with leading indicators like stage conversion rates and activity-to-outcome ratios, not just quota attainment. Middle performers offer the highest return on coaching investment because small improvements translate directly into revenue gains. Ambition gives managers a unified view of rep performance so you can identify coaching needs before the quarter is on the line. Skill gap heatmaps reveal where each rep needs targeted development rather than generic feedback. Structured coaching cadences prevent development from slipping when the quarter gets busy. Why Coaching Prioritization Matters for Revenue Teams Frontline managers directly influence 70% of team engagement and output. Your coaching decisions ripple across every deal in the pipeline. When you invest time with the right rep at the right moment, you protect revenue. When you miss the signal, deals slip quietly into the loss column. The challenge is that most managers operate without a clear prioritization framework. According to research from Gallup , managers who receive structured support around their coaching responsibilities see measurable improvements in team retention and engagement. The same principle applies to your reps: structured prioritization keeps coaching focused and impactful. What Gets in the Way of Effective Coaching Prioritization? Three common biases derail coaching prioritization. Recognizing them is the first step toward building a better system. Visibility Bias You coach the reps you see. Top performers often run more escalation calls and deal reviews, putting them in front of you more frequently. Meanwhile, middle-tier reps handle deals that look fine on the surface and receive less attention, even when their discovery or closing skills need work. Recency Bias A rep who lost a large deal last week gets a coaching session. A rep who has been losing smaller deals at a steady rate for months receives nothing, because no single loss triggered a review. Recency bias masks gradual performance decline. Outcome Bias Win/loss outcomes lag the behaviors that caused them by weeks or months. By the time you see a win rate drop in the numbers, the habits behind it have already compounded across dozens of calls. Coaching should target leading indicators, but most managers only see lagging ones. How to Identify Which Reps Need Coaching First Effective prioritization requires a shift from gut feel to data. The following signals help you build a prioritization system that surfaces coaching needs before they become performance gaps. Stage-Level Conversion Drop-Off Two reps with the same overall win rate can have completely different problems. One converts discovery to demo at 60% but demo to proposal at 30%. The other shows the inverse pattern. Stage-level conversion data tells you exactly which call type or skill to coach. Low discovery-to-demo conversion often signals qualification or pain identification issues. Low demo-to-proposal conversion points toward presentation skills or objection handling. Low proposal-to-close rates suggest negotiation or pricing confidence gaps. Win Rate Variance vs. Team Median A rep closing at 18% on a team with a 25% median has a 7-point gap worth investigating. The team median, not an arbitrary benchmark, is what flags individual reps for attention. Track this variance over rolling periods to catch trends before they become crises. Sales Cycle Length Variance Reps whose deals take 30% longer than the team median often have a discovery problem. They didn't qualify out early, didn't surface the real decision criteria, or didn't multi-thread fast enough. Segment by deal size before drawing conclusions, as strategic deals naturally take longer. Activity-to-Outcome Ratios The relationship between specific activities (discovery calls, demos, proposals) and closed deals reveals which behaviors drive revenue for each rep. A rep making more calls but closing fewer deals needs different coaching than a rep with strong conversion but low activity volume. The Performance Signals That Predict Coaching Needs Leading indicators let you intervene before the quarter closes. Focus on these signals to build a proactive coaching system. Talk-to-Listen Ratio Top performers typically land around 43% talk time on discovery calls. Reps consistently above 65% are pitching instead of discovering. This metric requires call recording and transcription to measure at scale, but it provides actionable insight into conversational habits. Question Quality and Depth The number of questions matters less than the type. A rep asking 12 closed-ended questions is interviewing. A rep asking 6 open-ended questions followed by 6 thoughtful follow-ups is doing real discovery. Score question type against your sales methodology to identify coaching opportunities. Objection Handling Patterns Track whether reps deflect, defer, or address objections directly. A rep who consistently loses momentum after pricing objections needs different coaching than one who falters on competitive displacement questions. Pattern recognition across calls reveals specific skill gaps. Follow-Up Consistency A rep can run a strong demo, agree to send a proposal by Friday, and never send it. The deal quietly drifts from live to ghosted without anyone noticing for weeks. Follow-up consistency is often a workflow problem rather than a coaching problem, but it still requires manager attention. Building a Rep Prioritization Framework With the right signals in place, you can build a repeatable framework for coaching prioritization. The goal is to identify which reps need your time this week, not just this quarter. Step 1: Establish Your Performance Baselines Calculate team medians for your key metrics: win rate, stage conversion rates, sales cycle length, and activity-to-outcome ratios. These baselines become your reference points for identifying variance. Update them quarterly to account for market changes and team composition shifts. Step 2: Segment Your Team by Performance Quartile Divide your team into four groups based on quota attainment and leading indicators. Your top quartile often needs less coaching time. Your bottom quartile may need performance management rather than coaching. The middle two quartiles, your "moveable middle," typically offer the highest return on coaching investment. Step 3: Map Skill Gaps to Specific Metrics For each rep below the team median on a given metric, identify the underlying skill gap. Low discovery-to-demo conversion might indicate weak qualification skills. Long sales cycles might reveal stakeholder mapping gaps. Specificity drives better coaching conversations. Step 4: Prioritize by Impact and Coachability Not every skill gap deserves equal attention. Prioritize gaps that directly affect revenue (stage conversions over activity volume) and focus on reps who demonstrate coachability through responsiveness and effort. A willing middle performer often delivers faster results than a resistant underperformer. How Ambition Helps Managers Prioritize Coaching Building a prioritization framework manually requires hours of spreadsheet work each week. Ambition's Coaching Orchestration automates the diagnostic work so you can focus on the conversation instead of the data collection. Ambition surfaces early indicators inside both conversations and pipeline movement, enabling you to course-correct sooner and eliminate surprises. The platform generates AI-powered coaching pre-reads that highlight which reps need attention this week based on performance signals, not just quota standing. Skill gap heatmaps show exactly where each rep needs targeted development. Productivity quadrants help you distinguish between reps who are busy and reps who are productive. Pipeline snapshots surface at-risk deals before they slip, giving you the context to coach around real opportunities rather than abstract skills. The "Move the Middle" Strategy for Coaching Prioritization The most reliable path to revenue improvement is focusing on your middle performers. Top performers are already producing. Bottom performers may need performance management or role changes. Middle performers offer the highest value for coaching investment. Why Middle Performers Deliver the Highest ROI A 10% improvement in your top performer's output is valuable but represents marginal gains. The same 10% improvement across five middle performers compounds into significant revenue lift. Middle performers also tend to be more coachable because they're hungry for development but not yet discouraged by persistent underperformance. Identifying Your Moveable Middle Your moveable middle consists of reps who are meeting some targets but missing others, or who show inconsistent performance across quarters. They have the skills to succeed but need targeted support to become consistent. Look for reps with high activity but lower conversion, or strong discovery scores but weaker closing metrics. Creating a Structured Coaching Cadence Prioritization without structure falls apart when the quarter gets busy. Build coaching into your operating rhythm so it doesn't become optional. Weekly 1:1 Structure Reserve 30-45 minutes weekly for each direct report. Use the first segment for deal review, the middle for skill development tied to their specific metrics, and the final segment for action items and accountability. Structured 1:1s prevent coaching from devolving into pipeline updates. Monthly Skill Focus Each month, identify one skill gap to work on with each rep. A rep cannot fix talk-to-listen ratio, question quality, and objection handling in the same week. Sequential focus produces better results than scattered attention. Re-measure the target metric at the end of the month to validate progress. Quarterly Performance Reviews Use quarterly reviews to reassess your prioritization framework. Reps move between quartiles. Skill gaps shift as reps develop. A static prioritization list becomes outdated quickly. Treat your framework as a living system that adapts to team changes. Measuring Coaching Effectiveness Coaching only matters if it produces results. Track these indicators to ensure your prioritization framework is working. Metric Movement After Coaching If you coached a rep on discovery-to-demo conversion, did that metric improve over the following 30 days? If not, either the diagnosis was wrong or the coaching approach needs adjustment. Metric movement is the most direct measure of coaching effectiveness. Rep Confidence and Engagement Effective coaching should increase rep confidence, not just compliance. Check whether reps are applying new skills proactively or only when reminded. Engagement surveys and informal check-ins reveal whether coaching is landing or creating friction. Coaching Coverage and Consistency Track how much coaching time each rep receives relative to their need. Are your highest-priority reps getting proportionally more attention? Are 1:1s happening consistently, or do they slip during busy periods? Coaching coverage data helps you audit your own prioritization discipline. Common Coaching Prioritization Mistakes to Avoid Even with a solid framework, certain pitfalls can undermine your prioritization efforts. Watch for these patterns in your own coaching practice. Overinvesting in Top Performers High performers are often the most enjoyable to coach because they respond quickly and produce visible results. But they also need your time least. Resist the pull toward coaching comfort and redirect attention to reps with higher development upside. Ignoring Workflow Problems Some performance gaps aren't skill gaps. A rep with poor CRM hygiene may be overwhelmed by six back-to-back calls with no time to update records. Before diagnosing a coaching need, rule out workflow and tooling issues that better systems could solve. Coaching Too Many Skills at Once A rep receiving feedback on five different skills will improve on none of them. Focus coaching efforts on one metric at a time, validate improvement, then move to the next priority. Depth beats breadth in skill development. Letting Busy Quarters Derail Development The end-of-quarter push is exactly when reps need coaching most, not least. Deals in motion create real-time teaching moments. Protect your coaching cadence during busy periods rather than canceling 1:1s to focus on deal support. Putting It All Together: Your Coaching Prioritization Checklist Use this weekly checklist to ensure your coaching time goes where it matters most. Review team performance data against established baselines. Identify reps more than 20% below the team median on any key metric. Map each underperformance signal to a specific skill gap. Prioritize middle performers who show coachability and high revenue impact. Prepare 1:1 agendas with specific metrics and skill focus areas. Track coaching coverage to ensure high-priority reps receive appropriate attention. Measure metric movement monthly to validate coaching effectiveness. In Conclusion: How to Build a Coaching Prioritization System That Drives Revenue Effective coaching prioritization starts with data, not instinct. By tracking leading indicators like stage conversion rates, activity-to-outcome ratios, and skill-specific metrics, you can identify which reps need your time before performance gaps become revenue problems. Focus your coaching investment on the moveable middle, where small improvements compound into significant revenue gains. Build structured cadences that protect development time even during busy quarters. And measure your effectiveness through metric movement, not just coaching activity. With Ambition , you can automate the diagnostic work and spend your time on what matters: helping your reps become better sellers. The platform delivers AI-powered coaching pre-reads, skill gap heatmaps, and pipeline intelligence that surface coaching priorities without hours of manual data analysis. Your reps deserve coaching that's targeted to their actual needs. Your revenue targets depend on it. FAQs about How to Prioritize Sales Coaching in 2026 How do I know which sales reps need coaching first? Start by identifying reps who fall more than 20% below your team median on key metrics like stage conversion rates, win rate, or sales cycle length. Ambition helps you surface these signals automatically through performance scorecards and skill gap heatmaps, so you can prioritize coaching without manual data analysis. What metrics should I track to prioritize coaching effectively? Focus on leading indicators rather than lagging outcomes. Stage-level conversion rates, activity-to-outcome ratios, talk-to-listen ratio, and sales cycle variance all predict performance gaps before they affect quota attainment. These metrics reveal which specific skills need development. Why should I focus coaching on middle performers? Middle performers offer the highest return on coaching investment. They have the foundational skills to succeed but need targeted support to become consistent. Ambition's Productivity Quadrant helps you identify these reps and track their improvement over time. How often should I reassess my coaching priorities? Review your prioritization framework monthly and update performance baselines quarterly. Reps move between performance quartiles as they develop or face new challenges. A static prioritization list becomes outdated quickly and misses emerging coaching opportunities. What's the biggest mistake managers make in coaching prioritization? Overinvesting in top performers is the most common mistake. High performers are enjoyable to coach and respond quickly, but they need your time least. Redirecting that attention to your moveable middle delivers higher revenue impact across the team.

title: Onboard.io Now Supports MCP: Connect Your Onboarding Data to AI Agents
summary: Onboard.io now supports MCP, letting AI tools like Claude connect to your live onboarding data to answer cross-system questions no dashboard was built for.
body_text: Onboard.io now supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) , the open standard that lets AI agents like Claude and ChatGPT connect directly to your onboarding data, managing and updatingreading projects, drafting client emails, scheduling meetings, and flagging at-risk accounts, all inside the AI tools your team already uses. The hardest part of onboarding isn't the work. It's the busywork around it. Customer Success teams don't lose time because onboarding is hard. They lose it to the overhead around it, the reporting, the cross-checking, and the constant reassembling of context that no single tool hands you ready-made. The answer to a simple question, like which clients need attention today, is rarely in one place. It's spread across your onboarding platform, your CRM, your inbox, and your calendar. Multiply that by a portfolio of 30, 40 or more accounts being onboarded and a real share of the day goes to stitching systems together by hand instead of spending time with the clients themselves. The costs are predictable: Manual reporting. A weekly status rollup or executive scorecard means exporting from several systems and stitching them together by hand. Slow follow-through. You know a client is slipping. Turning that into a sent email, a booked call, and a logged note still takes a dozen clicks across a dozen tabs. Scattered context. The full picture of a client is spread across your CRM, inbox, calendar, and files. Assembling it for even one account takes minutes you repeat dozens of times a day. The information needed to move faster already exists. It's just spread across tools that don't talk to each other. That's the gap MCP closes, across your platforms. What is the Onboard.io MCP integration? The Onboard.io MCP integration lets any MCP-compatible AI tool securely connect to your Onboard.io account and work with your live onboarding data, managing projects, tasks, phases, and client status, and taking actions like posting updates or drafting communications on your behalf. What is MCP? The Model Context Protocol is an open standard introduced by Anthropic in November 2024 that lets AI tools securely connect to external software and data sources. Think of it as a universal plug that lets an AI tool like Claude communicate with your business applications, reading data, taking actions, and working across platforms the way a skilled human assistant would. Because MCP is an open standard with a publicly available specification , the integration isn't tied to a single AI vendor. It works with any MCP-compatible tool. Throughout this post we use Claude and ChatGPT as the examples, since they offer native connector support you can set up from their settings panel without developer configuration, but the same integration works with other MCP-enabled platforms, and more are adopting the standard over time. What your team can do with it Once Onboard.io is connected alongside your other tools, the AI you already use, like Claude, can complete work in seconds that used to take 20 to 45 minutes of manual assembly: Help manage your onboarding projects within Onboard.io - the MCP is tooled to support frequent activities (e.g. updating tasks), which can be done with your approval. Generate a portfolio status report across every active onboarding project, with completion percentage and current phase. Draft personalized client emails using real contact names, tasks, and go-live dates, not generic templates. Surface at-risk projects that are stalled or behind schedule, with the business impact and a recommended next step. Build a client health scorecard that merges onboarding progress with deal values from your CRM into a single Green/Yellow/Red view. Schedule milestone meetings based on each project's phase, with a video link and a tailored agenda. Ask questions that span your systems Onboard.io already automates the repeatable parts of onboarding: creating projects, managing document signing and forms, sending welcome sequences, scheduling milestones, keeping your CRM in sync. Those run on their own. What no automation can anticipate is the judgment call that depends on data from several systems at once. That's where the AI you already use fits. Because a tool like Claude can read your live Onboard.io data alongside your CRM and inbox, it answers questions that would otherwise mean opening three tools and piecing the answer together by hand. You type something like: For each of my onboardings, pull the deal value from the CRM, the completion status from Onboard, and the sentiment of the last few client emails, then tell me which accounts are the biggest risk to revenue. The answer doesn't live in any one place, so the AI pulls it together across your connected tools in one pass: Reads completion status from Onboard.io, where each active project stands and what's overdue or blocked. Pulls deal value from your CRM, how much revenue each account represents. Reads the sentiment of recent client emails, which relationships feel strained, hesitant, or quiet, regardless of what the project status says. Weighs the three together and hands you a ranked list of the accounts where revenue is most at risk, with the reason for each. That's the case a person would otherwise catch only by luck, or by spending an afternoon cross-checking systems account by account. The AI does it in seconds. Bringing it together Onboard.io keeps running the onboarding work you rely on: creating projects, sending sequences, tracking milestones, and syncing your CRM. Our MCP adds a layer on top, so the AI tools your team already uses, like Claude and ChatGPT, can read your live onboarding data alongside your other systems and answer the cross-system questions that no dashboard or automation was built for. Setup is a simple connector authorization, not a development project, and connections use OAuth 2.0 so you stay in control of what's shared. The result is faster answers, earlier signals, and less time spent stitching systems together by hand. See Onboard in Action: Book a Demo

title: Usher London - O2 Arena
summary: Usher lit up London’s O2 Arena with a high octane, roller-skating spectacle that celebrated his 30 year career. From jaw dropping choreography to soulful crowd singalongs, the R&B icon proved he's still the ultimate showman.
body_text: Usher Electrifies the O2 with a Roller-Skating, Hit-Filled Spectacle Three decades into his career, Usher proved at London’s O2 Arena that he’s not just still got it, he owns it. Opening his ten-night residency with a spectacular show that mixed nostalgia, charisma, and sheer athleticism, the legenary R&B superstar delivered a two hour masterclass in entertainment that had the crowd in the palm of his hand from start to finish. From the moment the lights dimmed and futuristic visuals flashed across the giant screens, it was clear Usher wasn’t here to phone it in. A short montage revisiting his early days, baggy jeans and '90s era sunglasses reminded the audience of just how far he’s come. But once the man himself stepped onstage, there was no looking back. Dressed in a shimmering suit worthy of a Vegas headliner, he launched into his hits with the slick precision of the legend that he is. Gliding across the stage during a sizzling medley of Southern classics, Usher delivered flawless vocals while pulling off tight choreography on wheels. Fashion was a show of its own. Throughout the night, Usher switched between a leather biker get-up, a floor length fur coat, and an MJ inspired ensemble dripping with sequins. Each look seemed to channel a different era of his career, along with a different kind of vibe. Crowd favourites like “Confessions Part II” and “U Got It Bad” blew the roof off, with thousands singing every word! During the slow jams, the energy shifted from high octane to hypnotic, and Usher took his time, often speaking directly to the audience and turning the arena into an intimate, emotional space. By the end, it wasn’t just a concert... it was a reminder that Usher Raymond remains one of the most captivating performers in modern music. Still smooth. Still electric. And still skating circles around the competition.

title: Delcath Systems to Host Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Call
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Delcath Systems, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Delcath Systems to Host Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Call July 23, 2026 PDF Version QUEENSBURY, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 23, 2026-- Delcath Systems, Inc. (Nasdaq: DCTH), an interventional oncology company focused on the treatment of primary and metastatic cancers of the liver, announced today it will host a conference call on August 6, 2026, at 8:30 AM Eastern Time to discuss results for its second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Conference Call Information To participate in this event, dial in approximately 5 to 10 minutes before the beginning of the call. Event Date: Thursday, August 6, 2026 Time: 8:30 AM Eastern Time Participant Numbers: Toll Free: 1-800-717-1738 International: 1-646-307-1865 Webcast: https://viavid.webcasts.com/starthere.jsp?ei=1767384&tp_key=cbc23b55c8 A replay of the webinar will be available shortly after the conclusion of the call and will be archived on the company's website here . About Delcath Systems, Inc., HEPZATO KIT and CHEMOSAT Delcath Systems, Inc. is an interventional oncology company focused on the treatment of primary and metastatic liver cancers. The company's proprietary products, HEPZATO KIT™ (Hepzato (melphalan) for Injection/Hepatic Delivery System) and CHEMOSAT® Hepatic Delivery System for Melphalan percutaneous hepatic perfusion (PHP), are designed to administer high-dose chemotherapy to the liver while controlling systemic exposure and associated side effects during a PHP procedure. In the United States, HEPZATO KIT is considered a combination drug and device product and is regulated and approved for sale as a drug by the FDA. HEPZATO KIT is comprised of the chemotherapeutic drug melphalan and Delcath's proprietary Hepatic Delivery System (HDS). The HDS is used to surgically isolate the liver while simultaneously filtrating hepatic venous blood during melphalan infusion and washout. The use of the HDS results in loco-regional delivery of a relatively high melphalan dose, which can potentially induce a clinically meaningful tumor response with minimal hepatotoxicity and reduce systemic exposure. HEPZATO KIT is approved in the United States as a liver-directed treatment for adult patients with metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM) with unresectable hepatic metastases affecting less than 50% of the liver and no extrahepatic disease, or extrahepatic disease limited to the bone, lymph nodes, subcutaneous tissues, or lung that is amenable to resection or radiation. Please see the full Prescribing Information , including BOXED WARNING for the HEPZATO KIT. In Europe, the device-only configuration of the HDS is regulated as a Class III medical device and is approved for sale under the trade name CHEMOSAT Hepatic Delivery System for Melphalan, or CHEMOSAT, where it has been used in the conduct of percutaneous hepatic perfusion procedures at major medical centers to treat a wide range of cancers of the liver. title: Rakı-Balık Analizi #mindshare #brandequity #competitiveanalysis
summary: Rakı Nedir, Ne ile Gider, Türkiye’deki Konumu Nedir?
body_text: Rakı, genel anlamda bakıldığı zaman en çok bilinen Türk içkilerinden biridir. Tarihsel olarak ilk basit formu 11.yy’da Anadolu’da bulunmuştur. Ancak, kaynaklara bakıldığı zaman rakının günümüzde bilinen halinin 15.yy’a dayandığı görülür. Rakının en genel üç hammaddesi ise anason, üzüm ve sudur. Göreceli olarak sert bir içki olduğundan dolayı suyla birlikte tüketilir. Rakının bir felsefesinin olduğunu söylemek yanlış olmaz. Tarihsel süreçte rakıya bakıldığı zaman müzisyenlerden şairlere, yazarlardan sanatçılara, işçi sınıfından burjuvaziye kadar insanları bağladığı ve ortak paydada buluşturduğu görülecektir. Özellikle bazı Türk şairler üzerinde rakı felsefesinin fazlaca etkisi olduğu söylenebilir. Örneğin Orhan Veli, Sait Faik, Melih Cevdet, Edip Cansever ve Cemal Süreya, rakı hakkında yazmış veya arkadaşlarıyla rakı içmeyi sevdiği bilinen şairlerden bazılarıdır. Rakı, sadece bir içki olarak değil, aynı zamanda bir kültür olarak da insanların karşısına çıkar. Dahası, rakının içildiği özel mekanlar vardır ve bunlar da meyhane olarak adlandırılır. Meyhaneler, insanların birbirleriyle keyifle vakit geçirmeleri için tasarlanmış, isteğe göre müzik de dinlenebilen yerlerdir. Rakının sadece meze ile mi yendiği, yoksa rakının yemekle mi yenmesi gerektiği, rakıyı sevenlerin anlaşmazlığa düştüğü iki konudur. Bazıları rakının yanında sadece meze yerken, bazıları ise yemek yemeyi tercih edebilir. Fakat bir konu vardır ki, genelde herkes hemfikirdir, o da rakının yanında en iyi giden yemeğin balık olduğudur. Hatta Türkçe’de bu bir deyimdir: rakı balık yapmak. Rakıyı seven insanlar, rakının yanında balığı sevdiklerini ve bunun çok farklı bir hissiyatının ve keyfinin olduğunu düşünürler. Hangi balığın seçileceği ise bulunulan mevsime göre değişiklik gösterebilir. Genelde en taze ve mevsiminde olan balık ilk tercih edilendir. eBrandValue platformunun "Monitor" özelliği kullanılarak, sosyal medyada Ocak 2020 yılından günümüze, Rakı ile birlikte hangi balık türünün konuşulduğu analiz edildi. Sosyal medyada, tüketicilerin Rakıyla birlikte, Balık türü olarak eşlikçi tercihi sırasıyla kalamar, karides, levrek, çipura ve lüfer . Toplulukların fikirlerini anlamlandırmak ve onların seveceği eşleşmeler bulmak markaların önemli ihtiyaçlarından biridir. Bu doğrultuda markaların daha iyi kararlar vermesini sağlayan eBrandValue, şirketlerin benzersiz hizmetler sunması için müşterilerini daha iyi tanımalarına yardımcı olur. title: AI ROI starts when your agents can see how work really happens
summary: AI ROI improves when agents can see how work actually happens. Learn how process and task mining turn insights into action.
body_text: Imagine hiring a brilliant new employee and blindfolding them on day one. That’s how most enterprises deploy AI agents today. Agents decide without seeing the process AI agents are good at executing whatever task sits in front of them. What most deployments are missing is process intelligence, a live view of how work actually flows. An agent can’t tell you why one loan clears in six days while a nearly identical one takes 26. It doesn’t know that a third of your cases keep cycling back through a document step that should run once. Nobody gave it that information, so it decides without it, and the return on your AI spend shrinks accordingly. Dashboards find problems after you’ve paid for them Most organizations already collect the data that would catch this. It usually ends up in dashboards and quarterly reviews, which means someone looks at it weeks or months after the damage started. Then a team still has to agree on a fix and ship it. On a good day that takes a quarter. Here are the numbers from one real loan origination process. Out of 17,436 cases, 30% needed rework. The biggest single cause was a document collection loop that trapped 17% of all cases and added roughly 20 days to each one. None of this was hidden. The evidence sat in the event logs the whole time. The people working those loans had no way to see it. A smartwatch for your AI agents Pega Process and Task Mining shows how work actually gets done. Process Mining reads event logs from enterprise systems and maps how processes really run. Task Mining records desktop activity, which catches the manual workarounds that never reach a system log. Gartner named Pega a Leader in its 2026 Magic Quadrant for Process Intelligence Platforms . The new part is who can use that intelligence. Through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an agent queries it live, in the middle of handling a case. It works like a smartwatch reading your heart rate mid-run: live measurements, delivered while there’s still time to do something about them. An agent handling a loan can pull up the stall patterns from similar cases and reroute before the same thing happens again. Most process mining tools stop at the insight. Pega Process and Task Mining connects the findings to Pega Blueprint , which redesigns the workflow and pushes the change into execution. The gap between knowing about a problem and fixing it shrinks from months to hours. Three takeaways for leaders Context is the bottleneck. Your agents already reason well. What they’re missing is visibility into how work flows, and that’s where the next round of AI ROI comes from. Process intelligence becomes operational infrastructure. It moves out of quarterly reviews and into the live decision path of every agent. The closed loop is the advantage. Process Mining finds the issues, agents act on them, and Pega Blueprint redesigns the workflow. A tool that stops at the dashboard can only tell you what already went wrong. From doing tasks to improving work Most AI systems execute tasks. Improving the process itself is rarer, and it’s the part that compounds. An agent that can see how work happens learns something from every case it touches. If you’re deciding where the next AI dollar goes, give the agents you already have a way to see the process they work in. For a closer look, read how process mining and task mining work together.
